Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding Virginia Code § 58.1-339.8 and the refundable credit for 2026:

For taxable years beginning on and after January 1, 2025 but before January 1, 2027, any individual or married individuals filing jointly may claim a refundable credit against tax in an amount equal to 20 percent of the credit claimed by the individual or married individuals for federal individual income taxes.

For Tax Years 2025 and 2026, the refundable portion of the Virginia Earned Income Tax Credit increases from 15% to 20%.

This means that for the 2026 taxable year, Virginia taxpayers who are eligible for the federal Earned Income Tax Credit can claim a refundable credit equal to 20% of their federal EITC under § 58.1-339.8. The credit is refundable, so it can be more than the total amount of your tax.

input.summary: Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(3) lets a filer claim a refundable credit for taxable years 2025 and 2026. The credit equals 20% of the federal § 32 EITC and is taken in place of the nonrefundable low-income credit and the nonrefundable EITC. The head is 40 and has no children, so the federal EITC is 7.65% × $520 = $39.78, which gives $7.96 for Virginia. The engine's steps match this, and stage 1 reached the same figure. The consensus answer of $0 rests on the wrong belief that the credit is nonrefundable or has expired. The only open point is rounding: the IRS lookup table gives an EITC of $40, which would make the Virginia credit $8.00.
